name: Will replacing my kitchen countertops damage my existing tile backsplash?

mainEntity.name: Will replacing my kitchen countertops damage my existing tile backsplash?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing countertops usually disrupts your existing backsplash, particularly if the old counter had an attached four-inch lip or if tiles were set directly onto the deck. Removing old counters often tears drywall paper or chips lower tiles. Many homeowners take this opportunity to install a full-height tile backsplash that coordinates with the new slab. If you intend to keep your current tile, prepare for careful demo and subsequent drywall patching or grout repairs along the joint.
acceptedAnswer.description: It often causes minor damage to adjacent tile or drywall. While careful removal helps, installing a fresh tile backsplash after new counters go in usually yields the cleanest look.
